title: Agents Without Code: Skills, YAML, and Filesystems Replaced Python — Philipp Schmid, Google DeepMind
talk_summary: Speaker demos the same GitHub PR review agent as raw Python, an agent framework, then a remote sandbox agent configured by agents.md/skills.md and general bash/GitHub CLI tools. Main claim: as models improve, replace bespoke orchestration and tool schemas with files, general tools, sandbox credential proxying, and file-based context handoff.

takeaways.technique: General CLI/filesystem tools instead of bespoke tool schemas
takeaways.what_they_do: Inside a sandbox, the agent gets bash, filesystem, and GitHub CLI; it installs gh if missing and uses existing CLI knowledge to review PRs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we just tell the agent, hey, you have a GitHub CLI, you have a bash tool, you have file systems.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instructions and rules live in agents.md; new capabilities are added as skills.md files, so extending the agent does not require changing code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we write a skills MD file maybe with some additional information on which CLI tool to use

takeaways.what_they_do: A network proxy around the sandbox injects credentials on outbound requests and can restrict allowed domains, so the agent never sees tokens.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent never really sees your credential. It just knows hey I can call the GitHub API

takeaways.what_they_do: Agents write notes, preferences, or handoff state to files so later sessions can pick up long-running work without carrying all context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can like just write that information that hand off to a file and like tell the agent to later pick it up.

takeaways.what_they_do: Remove custom orchestration/tool code when general tools and better models suffice; the talk cites Cursor replacing ~12k TypeScript lines with ~200 lines of agent files and Worsel removing 80% of tools.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if your harness is getting more complex as the model improves, you are most likely overengineering your harness.
takeaways.numbers: Cursor: ~12,000 lines TypeScript replaced by ~200 lines agent files; Worsel removed 80% of tools

takeaways.technique: Own domain evals and verify outcomes
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of micromanaging execution paths, focus on domain instructions, workflows, clean tools, and especially evals that verify outcomes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Own what is yours meaning focus on your domain instructions. Focus on the workflows. Focus especially on the evals
